summary: The per-scope assignment substrate (cinatra#2813 S1, epic #2812) — the operator-upgrade twin of four fresh-install bootstrap halves widened in the SAME PR: agentAssignedSkillsSchemaQueries (src/lib/skill-lifecycle-schema.ts), the new agentAssignedContextSchemaQueries (src/lib/agent-assigned-context-schema.ts), the agent_runs column entry (src/lib/drizzle-store.ts) and assistantThreadSchemaQueries (src/lib/assistant-thread-schema.ts). WHY: the epic assigns skills and context artifacts per agent PER SCOPE, and the landed store is package-global — one set of assigned skills per agent, everywhere — so the row identity widens from (package, skill) to (package, skill, scope_kind, scope_id) and the position slot the cap rides on widens with it. FOUR CHANGES: agent_assigned_skills gains scope_kind, scope_id, source and a forward-looking origin_run_id (ON DELETE SET NULL — deleting a run loses the POINTER, never the assignment a person kept); the new agent_assigned_context table keys on (package, slot, artifact, scope_kind, scope_id) with the artifact FK ON DELETE CASCADE, because an artifact that no longer exists cannot stay attached to an agent; agent_runs and assistant_threads each gain the immutable assignment_scope_snapshot jsonb column, so a run's applicable scopes are decided once at creation and the MUTABLE assistant_threads.project_id can never supply assignment scope. EXISTING ROWS BECOME WORKSPACE ROWS: a package-global assignment is by definition one that applied everywhere, and workspace is the tier that still means that, so nothing is lost and nothing is invented; every pre-existing row is source manual, because the only writer that existed was a person on the settings page. The scope CHECKs are built by src/lib/assignment-scope.ts and spliced into both tables in both of their homes so the four copies of the rule cannot drift. The position slot index is replaced under a NEW name rather than created IF NOT EXISTS, because keeping the narrow index would refuse a second scope's first assignment. Idempotent throughout — every statement is IF NOT EXISTS or a DO block that inspects the catalog first — so this is a no-op on a database the bootstrap already created wide. Recorded as destructive because the classifier enumerates a PRIMARY KEY change and an index replacement as such; no row is deleted by the forward migration. DOWN narrows back and DELETES every non-workspace row first, because the narrow key cannot hold two scoped rows for one (package, skill) — the truthful revert of 'assignments became per-scope'. SEQ 0100 — strictly greater than the max shipped seq on the default branch (core__0099). migrations/** is HIGH-RISK: maintainer approval required; the lane never merges.
